nextStoryContext: US-R2-001 (CAM-479 review-round fix) fixed a CRITICAL production bug in makeEarlyDeathProbe (src/supervisor/early-death.ts): the closure-local `samples` Map was overwritten unconditionally on every call (`samples.set(uuid, currentSample)` ran regardless of whether the transcript's byte size had changed), so the stored 'previous' sample was always exactly one poll tick (5_000 ms, DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS/DEFAULT_REVIEW_POLL_INTERVAL_MS/DEFAULT_PLAN_POLL_INTERVAL_MS) old on the next call. Since currentSample.timestamp - previousSample.timestamp was therefore always ~5_000 ms and EARLY_DEATH_FLOOR_MS is 60_000 ms, the elapsedMs < floorMs guard in classifyEarlyDeath returned 'still-working' on every tick forever, meaning the whole early-death detector (US-002/US-003/US-005 of the CAM-479 PRD) could never fire in production on any of the four dispatch loops (implementer, reviewer, planner, auditor), even though the pure core (classifyEarlyDeath) and the existing stateful-probe unit tests both looked correct in isolation (those tests only ever called the probe TWICE, jumping the injected clock by the whole floor window in one step -- a cadence no production caller uses, which is exactly why the bug shipped past a green 5911-test suite). Fix: the stored sample is now a freeze ANCHOR, not a sliding 'last observation' -- it is only replaced when the transcript's byte size actually changes (or there is no prior sample yet); when the size is unchanged across a call, the OLD sample (with its original timestamp) is kept as both the anchor AND the value passed as `previousSample` into classifyEarlyDeath, so the measured frozen window accumulates across consecutive same-size ticks instead of resetting to one poll interval on every call. Verification: added a NEW regression test ('regression (US-R2-001): a frozen dead-on-first-turn transcript still fires across many production-cadence poll ticks', test/supervisor/dispatch-early-death.test.ts) that replays the REAL probe against the real dead-on-first-turn fixture at the actual production 5_000 ms poll cadence for up to 480 ticks (40 simulated minutes); confirmed by hand that this exact test FAILS (fired=false) against the pre-fix code (git stash of early-death.ts only) and PASSES against the fix. This is the same reproduction shape the story's own review artifact used (scripts/cam/review-artifact.txt section 3, 'fired at: NEVER' before, fires within the floor window after). Also appended a docstring clarification to makeEarlyDeathProbe explaining the anchor semantics. Note: prd.json (present in the working tree at session start, modified by the review round that filed this story) also carries a sibling story US-R2-002 ('No test drives the real probe at the cadence the production loops call it') asking for exactly the kind of production-cadence regression test this story's fix already added as its own verification artifact; that story was NOT self-selected or closed here (out of scope per this agent's mandate to implement only its assigned story), but whoever picks up US-R2-002 next should first check whether the new regression test already added in this commit (test/supervisor/dispatch-early-death.test.ts, 'makeEarlyDeathProbe (stateful)' describe block) satisfies its acceptance criteria before writing a duplicate one; if it does, US-R2-002 may reduce to a no-op / cross-reference rather than new test code (US-R2-002 also asks for a sibling case where the transcript grows every few ticks and never fires, which was NOT added here and would still be net-new). Quality gates run in full: bun run typecheck (clean), bun test (5912 pass/0 fail, includes the new regression test), and the full bun run check:all spine (typecheck/test/embed-vendor/lint/file-size/debt-markers/version-skips/coverage/dead-code/dup/ci-parity/agents-md/test-sleeps/skip-ratchet, all green, no ceiling raises needed -- the diff was small enough not to trip file-size or coverage floors).
